name: St. Francis of Assisi
finderPrompt: Walk with Francis when you want peace, simplicity, and love for creation.
sourceTradition: Medieval Franciscan tradition and Catholic calendars remember Francis as the founder of the Friars Minor and a witness to poverty, peace, and care for creation.
patronageRationale: His preaching of peace, simple living, and affection for creatures explains the links to animals, creation, and peacemaking.
devotionalNote: Stories about Francis preaching to birds and taming the wolf of Gubbio are beloved devotional traditions; present them as teaching stories rather than classroom historical proof.

name: St. Carlo Acutis
finderPrompt: Carlo is a good guide for students and anyone trying to use technology with holiness.
sourceTradition: Modern Church biographies remember Carlo for Eucharistic devotion, charity, and using web skills to share Eucharistic miracle research.
patronageRationale: His teenage witness, school life, and thoughtful use of computers support the student, technology, and young people tags.
devotionalNote: Carlo's cause is recent, so keep claims concrete and avoid implying an official patronage title beyond common devotional association.

name: St. Joseph
finderPrompt: Joseph helps when duty feels quiet, heavy, or deeply important.
sourceTradition: The Gospels name Joseph as Mary's husband and Jesus' foster father; Catholic devotion also honors him as a worker on May 1.
patronageRationale: His care for the Holy Family and his trade as a carpenter ground the family, fatherhood, and worker connections.

name: St. Therese of Lisieux
finderPrompt: Therese shows how small acts can become brave love.
sourceTradition: Therese's autobiography and Carmelite tradition shaped her 'little way' of trust, hidden love, and prayer for missionaries.
patronageRationale: Her hidden prayer for missions, long illness, and teaching on ordinary holiness explain the mission, sickness, and everyday holiness tags.

name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
finderPrompt: Kolbe is a courageous companion when love asks for sacrifice.
sourceTradition: Twentieth-century martyr accounts remember Kolbe's Marian devotion, publishing apostolate, and voluntary death in Auschwitz in another prisoner's place.
patronageRationale: His imprisonment and sacrifice connect him to prisoners and families, while his Catholic publishing work supports the media tag.
devotionalNote: When teaching children, keep the Auschwitz context age-appropriate and emphasize sacrificial love without graphic detail.

name: St. Bernadette Soubirous
finderPrompt: Bernadette helps when faith needs humility, honesty, and trust.
sourceTradition: Lourdes tradition and Church investigations remember Bernadette as the young visionary who reported apparitions of Mary and later lived religious life quietly.
patronageRationale: Her poverty, illness, pilgrim shrine at Lourdes, and experience of being doubted support the sickness, pilgrimage, and unseen tags.
devotionalNote: Marian apparition details belong to devotional tradition approved for belief; avoid presenting private revelation as required doctrine.

name: St. Padre Pio
finderPrompt: Padre Pio points hard days toward prayer, mercy, and perseverance.
sourceTradition: Modern Capuchin and Church records remember Padre Pio for prayer, confession, patient suffering, and spiritual counsel.
patronageRationale: His long ministry hearing confessions, reputation for intercession, and intense prayer life explain the confession, healing, and prayer tags.
devotionalNote: Miracle and stigmata stories are part of his devotional history; focus quests on prayer, mercy, and perseverance.

name: St. John Paul II
finderPrompt: John Paul II is a hopeful guide for courage, mercy, and big-hearted love.
sourceTradition: Recent papal teaching, World Youth Day history, and canonization records remember John Paul II's public witness to mercy, family life, youth, and peace.
patronageRationale: His outreach to young people, teaching on family dignity, and global peace witness support the young people, families, and world peace tags.
